messages:
Marta: Heads-up — Dedicated canary in us-west-2 showing ~2x p99 after last deploy, blocking the rollout. I saw SLA alerts from two customers.

infra-bot: [perf-alert] perf-tests/dedicated p95 ↑80% on merge abc123 (PR #4128). See run: https://ci.internal/runs/9876

Devon: quick skim of the flamegraph: https://perf.internal/flame/9876 — big hotspot in kernel_dispatch -> select_kernel for short sequence workloads.

Ryan: I repro locally with short-seq load; autokernel hinting is choosing the generic matmul fallback instead of the fused attention kernel on seq<=64. Latency jumps when KV cache warmups align with these short requests.

Anika: Also noticed batching heuristics changed in the same PR — the batch aggregator is delaying flushes waiting for larger batches, which pushes some tails into higher p99. PR #4128 touched batching thresholds and kernel selector ordering.

Marta: Customers are seeing user-facing slowdowns (chat features). SLOs/pager alerts fired. We should hold the Dedicated rollout until we have a mitigation.

SRE-Oncall: Putting the Dedicated rollout on hold now. Can someone bisect to pin the offending commit? infra-bot only flagged the merge commit.

Devon: Bisecting — narrowed it down to the merge that adjusted kernel priority: commit def456 (author jlee). That commit reorders fallback kernels and tweaks the `batch_timeout_ms` default.

Ryan: Quick experiment: reverted the fallback ordering locally (fused_attention > matmul) and ran load. p95 and p99 returned to baseline for short-seq tests. Command I used:
```
tools/perf/run --model=gpt-small --seq=32 --clients=32 --duration=120
```

Anika: There's an orthogonal issue: KV cache evictions spiked after the merge. Logs show `kv_cache_evictions` jumped from ~120 -> ~410 under similar load, which increases upstream fetch latency and amplifies the kernel mismatch effect.

Marta: Proposed plan: 1) hold Dedicated rollout (done), 2) open hotfix reverting kernel selector reorder + restore previous batching thresholds, 3) run hotpatch to canary, 4) notify affected customers and sales.

Devon: Opening PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/pr/4281 — includes revert of fallback ordering + batching tweak (set batch_timeout_ms back to 8ms). Running perf CI locally; will post results.

infra-bot: [perf-ci] PR 4281 results: p95 down ~30% vs bad merge, kv_cache_evictions reduced to ~140. Full perf report: https://ci.internal/runs/9888/report

SRE-Oncall: Good signals. Schedule hotpatch to the dedicated canary in the next 30m, oncall will watch traces and KV eviction metrics. If anything regresses, rollback immediately.

Ryan: Will follow up with deeper profiler traces to ensure long-seq fast paths are unaffected by the revert. Also adding a small unit test to pin kernel selection priority in CI.

Marta: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. If the hotpatch stabilizes, we can unhold the rollout and communicate ETA to customers. If not, escalate to eng-sre for a coordinated rollback and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
